added_models.model: Human CTLA4 knock-in (Ctla4h/h) mice dosed with ipilimumab, alone or with anti-PD-1

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 16037385). Not cited in the BLA 125377 pharmacology review text.
safety.note: Human CTLA4 knock-in mice built after melanoma irAEs were reported; anti-human CTLA-4 antibodies gave tumour rejection with mild autoimmunity, never set beside patient data.
safety.quote: we have generated human CTLA4 gene knock-in mice and used them to compare a panel of anti-human CTLA-4 antibodies for their ability to induce tumor rejection and autoimmunity.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use of the system. The paper was motivated by the melanoma irAE reports but states no side-by-side comparison; Du 2018 later says this adult-mouse version 'failed to recapitulate clinical observations' because its autoimmunity was mild, a judgement not available in 2005 (rule 7).

safety.magnitude_basis: organ pattern: mouse myocarditis, anaemia/red-cell aplasia and heart, lung, liver, kidney, gut inflammation vs patient grade 3-4 irAEs (colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis); no incidence or exposure comparison
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5939041). Severe irAEs required dosing perinatal mice (from birth, read at 6 weeks); 6-7-week-old adults showed milder heart and kidney lesions. Patient side is the paper's own citation of CheckMate 012 (NSCLC) and CheckMate 067 (melanoma); the NSCLC supplements to BLA 125377 were not read.
safety.note: Ipilimumab, alone and with anti-PD-1, gave perinatal knock-in mice severe multi-organ irAEs and red-cell aplasia, reproducing the irAE profile known from NSCLC and melanoma trials.
safety.short: Ipilimumab irAEs reproduced in humanised mice
safety.quote: In this model, the clinically used drug, Ipilimumab, induced severe irAE especially when combined with an anti-PD-1 antibody; whereas another mAb, L3D10, induced comparable CITE with very mild irAE under the same conditions.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction, so retro, never same: the model was tuned (perinatal dosing, anti-PD-1 combination) to reproduce irAEs known from melanoma since 2003 and from NSCLC combination cohorts (Hellmann 2017 CheckMate 012, 10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30624-6), both of which the paper cites as the patient side, so comparison_stated true and no import. Separate track from ctla4-knockout-mouse (loss of function, no antibody) and from the BLA hCTLA-4 transgenic tumour mice (efficacy prediction): different model and a different, product-level safety prediction. Match is in direction only; myocarditis and anaemia dominate the mouse, colitis and hepatitis the patients. Its forward prediction (L3D10/HL12 safer) has no patient test.

added_models.model: Ctla4+/- Pdcd1-/- compound mutant mice (genetic ICI-myocarditis model)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 33257470); full text not retrievable from Europe PMC within budget. Epub 2020-11-30, print March 2021.
safety.note: Compound mutant mice (one Ctla4 allele lost on a Pdcd1-null background) built to model myocarditis under combined CTLA-4 and PD-1 loss; no antibody is dosed.
safety.quote: Here, we report a robust preclinical mouse model of ICI-associated myocarditis in which monoallelic loss of Ctla4 in the context of complete genetic absence of Pdcd1 leads to premature death in approximately half of mice.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use, same year as its comparison. A different system from ctla4-knockout-mouse: heterozygous Ctla4 on a Pdcd1-null background, modelling the combination regimen's cardiac harm rather than complete CTLA-4 loss.

safety.magnitude_basis: myocardial T-cell and macrophage infiltration with ECG abnormalities, as in patient ICI myocarditis; the model's ~50% penetrance is a genetic dose, not a drug incidence
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the paper's patient side is ICI-myocarditis cases across cancers (its own abatacept case series and the literature), not an NSCLC cohort, hence imported from cancer (MONDO:0004992). Clinical myocarditis incidence is about 1%, so the match is qualitative.
safety.note: Mice lacking Pdcd1 and one Ctla4 allele died of T-cell and macrophage myocarditis with ECG changes, reproducing myocarditis reported on ipilimumab plus nivolumab since 2016.
safety.quote: Premature death results from myocardial infiltration by T cells and macrophages and severe ECG abnormalities, closely recapitulating the clinical and pathologic hallmarks of ICI-associated myocarditis observed in patients.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: built after fulminant myocarditis on ipilimumab plus nivolumab was reported (Johnson 2016 NEJM, melanoma), so retro, never same; the source states the comparison. Models the class's combination harm (ipilimumab plus anti-PD-1, the NSCLC regimen of CheckMate 227 and 9LA) without dosing any antibody, so product_in_model false. Direction only: the human comparison is organ and histology pattern, not incidence. Its forward prediction (abatacept rescue) was tested only in a case series, not scored.

considered_not_added: KEYNOTE-598, Lung-MAP S1400I and CheckMate 73L: patient-side results for the existing syngeneic-mouse-dual-blockade track, not new model systems; left to the draft's corrections.

Selby 2016 cynomolgus combination toxicology (dose-dependent GI inflammation with ipilimumab plus nivolumab): the draft already tracks cynomolgus-toxicology (contra, 2011); a 2016 entry belongs on that track, not in added_models.

Selby 2016 human-PBL ex-vivo assays (SEB superantigen and MLR cytokine release with ipilimumab plus nivolumab): the paper states only a melanoma efficacy comparison (CheckMate 067), which cannot be imported for efficacy (disease-only rule) and repeats the dual-blockade mice's prediction; no NSCLC patient cytokine or T-cell readout was found to set beside it. No admissible NSCLC comparison, so not added.

hCTLA-4 transgenic mice dosed with ipilimumab itself (BLA 125377 PharmR: SA1/N, MC-38, CT-26; study MDX-010-005-r): a different host and antibody but the same prediction as the Leach 1996 surrogate track (transplanted tumour rejection means the class works), compared with the same NSCLC trials; under this run's rule (different model and different prediction) it stays folded into syngeneic-mouse-surrogate-ctla4, where the draft already notes it. Du 2018's Ctla4h/h knock-in is added separately because its prediction is a product-level safety one.

Du 2018 Cell Res companion paper (10.1038/s41422-018-0011-0, Ctla4h/h mice: ipilimumab's tumour rejection is Fc/Treg-depletion dependent, not B7 blockade): a mechanism retrodiction with no patient-outcome comparison for NSCLC; not scored.

Human CTLA4 haploinsufficiency (Kuehn 2014 Science, Schubert 2014 Nat Med) as a human_genetic model of anti-CTLA-4 harm: neither discovery paper mentions ipilimumab or compares the phenotype with irAEs, and the only sources stating the parallel found within budget are reviews, which are not sources; a pairing would be entirely mine, so not added.

Gombos 2018 (AGEN1884/zalifrelimab monkey toxicology and human T-cell assays): the monkey system is already tracked as cynomolgus-toxicology, the paper states no patient comparison, and zalifrelimab has no NSCLC patient result (only cervical cancer trials surfaced).
Quavonlimab (MK-1308): no preclinical model paper surfaced; Perets 2021 (NSCLC Phase 1) is already discussed in the draft's engagement judgement.

Humanised-PDX NSCLC mice, patient-derived organoids / tumour fragments and QSP virtual trials: searches returned anti-PD-1-only NSCLC work (Meraz, NPRL2 2025), HCC and breast QSP models, or reviews; no NSCLC system dosed with an anti-CTLA-4 member and compared with patients was found.
